title: cobolwork/coverage
description: A SARIF property-bag convention for analyser coverage: what a run read, what it did not, and why it stopped. SARIF 2.1.0 can say that files could not be read, through invocations[].toolExecutionNotifications, but it has no standard way to state coverage as a ratio with a denominator. This is that denominator. It lives under invocations[].properties['cobolwork/coverage'], namespaced so it cannot be mistaken for a standard field, and it is an addition to the standard notifications rather than a replacement for them: a conforming consumer that ignores this key still learns which files were not read. It is published with one implementation, which is not enough to make it a standard. If a second analyser adopts it, the right venue is a proposed invocation.coverage object at the OASIS SARIF Technical Committee, where the bar is prior use rather than a good argument.

coverageIncomplete.description: True when the run did not read everything it selected. The verdict, and the reason this convention exists: a finding count over source nobody read is not a clean result. It is duplicated in invocations[].properties.coverageIncomplete and reflected in executionSuccessful, so a consumer cannot miss it by not knowing about this key.

filesScanned.description: Artifacts whose bytes were read by at least one analysis.

bySet.description: Per analysis component, keyed by the component's own name. A run whose components read different slices of the tree cannot state one number, and a single total hides which analysis fell short.

setsIncomplete.description: Components that did not fully run, each with the reason. Two distinct causes share this list and `kind` distinguishes them: a component that could not run for want of configuration, and one that ran and did not reach everything. Only `coverage` bears on whether the scan read what it was given.

kind.description: coverage: the component ran and did not read everything. configuration: it could not run in full because it was not told enough, such as a missing cobolwork.site.json.

why.description: Written for a person deciding what to do about it, from the reasons for that kind.

componentCoverage.description: filesScanned + filesNotRead + filesUnreadable + filesUnparsed accounts for every artifact the component selected.

filesUnreadable.description: Selected, and the bytes never arrived.

filesUnparsed.description: Read, and could not be parsed. Distinct from unreadable: counting these as unreadable understates what the run managed to look at.

filesNotRead.description: Selected and never opened, because the run stopped before reaching them.

stoppedBy.description: What ended the reading early, in the words of the limit that was hit.

unreadable.description: 'path: reason', one per artifact. A count names nothing anyone can go and look at, and it cannot tell a permission denied from the analyser being wrong.

notRead.description: One sentence a report can print verbatim, saying how much was missed and that the result is not a claim about the whole input.
